title: The 1944 Black & White solo piano record
summary: Details of a Cliff solo record made July 15, 1944, and how she announced it at the House.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Incidentally, can you tell us a little bit about that record.
Yeah. This record, it's recorded July 15, 1944 and it's a Black and White label and it was probably pressed or made in the city here and there's a company, 2117 Foster Avenue, Brooklyn, New York --

Foster Avenue, it's a Black and White label. This particular selection along with some others is out of Chuck Howze's collection -- Chuck Howze was a very devoted fan of Cliff's from down in Washington, D.C. He had quite a collection. At the time that the Howze jazz bill opened, Chuck Howze came up to New York and he brought these albums, these records with him -- incidentally it looks like an album because it's 12 inches, but we were -- I looked at it, it said, 'It Had to Be You' one solo and I pulled the album out and said it can't be, you know, the whole album, but it's actually 78. It's a large record.

thing with Bill Evans or Cecil Taylor.

Yeah, but when I looked and saw just one solo I figured it had to be 78. But anyway, we have in this collection a 78 that Cliff made in 1926 and one of the selections is "Maple Leaf Rag" of course, and the other one is "The Entertainer." And we had around the house there -- I didn't have anything to play it on, but we had a piano roll that Cliff made in 1926 called the "Hock Shop Blues" and I took it down to the Songwriter's Hall of Fame here in New York, which was at Number One Times Square and they have a player piano down there. It's electrified, of course, but we've got it up to the right speed and if was very fascinating to watch the piano roll and see the hole in the roll itself and then watch the keys go down, and I was saying, you know, you could use this piano roll as a teaching tool, because you could almost sit down and play after having watched this roll.
So it's down there now and in one of my announcements I announced the fact that it was at the Songwriter's Hall of Fame and anybody who

happened to be down there asked to hear it, and they'd be glad to play it for them. There is an album out with all piano rolls and of course that's how I knew that that piano roll was made in 1926. There's a list of piano rolls and the artists who made them. Fats Waller, Eubie Blake and others and it seems that Cliff made two piano rolls but they can't find but the one and that's the "Hockshop Blues."
